Subject: Dedicated capacity question — Mandrake production profile

Hey Monica / Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. We want to lock in dedicated capacity for our document-understanding API. A few specifics from our side:

- Typical request: 1k token prompt + 500 token generation (avg ~1.5k tokens).
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~60 reqs/min during business hours, with 10x microbursts (~600 reqs/min) lasting 30–90s, 2–3x/day.
- Desired SLO: p95 latency for end-to-end response <= 600ms.

Can Redwood map this to tokens/sec and suggest a slab/reserve recommendation and the expected p95 with/without KV cache warm? Also please call out headroom for bursts and fallback behaviour (degraded model/queueing) — procurement will want concrete numbers to evaluate the commitment.

Appreciate a short write-up + any attachments we can share with procurement.

—Samir

Samir —

Attaching a concise proposal for procurement with the commitments and fallback options. High-level commercial summary:

- Recommended reserved slab: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with burst-bucket for 2 additional GPUs for 3x/day microbursts.
- Monthly commit estimate: 18TB token capacity equivalent (see attached pdf for conversion).
- Pricing: blended committed rate + burst overage at 1.5x committed unit price.

Technical TL;DR (see Karthik's note for detailed latency math):
- Baseline mapping: 60 reqs/min * 1500 tokens = 90k tokens/min -> 1.5k tokens/sec sustained.
- Burst peak: 600 reqs/min * 1500 tokens = 900k tokens/min -> 15k tokens/sec peak for 30–90s.
- With the recommended 4-GPU slab (opt kernels + int8 quantization): expect p95 token-generation latency ~40–70ms/token substituting into model —~which maps to end-to-end p95 of ~350–500ms depending on KV cache warm state.
- Headroom: the reserved slab plus 2-GPU burst covers typical microburst without rolling to degraded fallback in 90% of observed traffic patterns; otherwise automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant reduces token latency by ~2–3x but increases model error slightly.

Attachments: mandrake_dedicated_proposal.pdf (commercial), runbook-mandrake.md (ops).

Next step: Monica / Karthik to send a short technical appendix that procurement can include with the proposal.

Thanks,

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Mandrake dedicated proposal (technical appendix + runbook)

Folks —

Posting a short technical appendix and an ops runbook excerpt below. I'm copying the essential math so procurement/ops have a clear signal on risk and mitigations.

=== Technical appendix (summary) ===
Assumptions:
- Model: 16k context LLM, optimized kernels, int8 quantized variant available (approx 2.5x throughput improvement vs fp16 at parity quality for many tasks).
- Token generation cost: measured on Redwood testbed: ~0.06ms per token per A100-equivalent in steady pipeline when fully batched; practical sustained per-GPU throughput ~6k tokens/sec with continuous batching for our decoders (16k context increases mem pressure but similar per-token time).

Conversion math:
- Baseline tokens/sec = 1500 tokens * 60 reqs/min / 60 = 1500 tokens/sec? Wait — correct calc: 60 reqs/min = 1 req/sec -> 1 * 1500 = 1500 tokens/sec baseline.
- Peak burst tokens/sec = 600 reqs/min = 10 req/sec -> 10 * 1500 = 15,000 tokens/sec peak.

GPU mapping:
- Effective per-GPU sustained throughput (accounting for KV cache miss and decoding overhead): 5.5k tokens/sec.
- Baseline (1.5k tps) -> ~0.3 GPU sustained (comfortably within 1 GPU).
- Target steady-state reserve of 4 GPUs -> 22k tps sustained capacity (5.5k*4). This covers baseline + typical microbursts with ~7k tokens/sec headroom left for queuing/other tenants.
- Burst coverage: adding 2 burst GPUs -> 33k tps capacity; peak 15k easily covered with margin (allows for degradation on cold cache).

Latency mapping:
- Per-token generation latency ~0.06 ms/token (ideal) -> for 1500 tokens generation = 90ms generation time; attention / KV overhead + beam/decoding overhead -> add 120–300ms depending on cache warm/cold -> end-to-end generation p95 ~210–390ms. Combine with network and pre/post-processing -> end-to-end p95 estimate 300–550ms.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- KV cache warm: implement async cache priming for long-tail documents during off-peak windows; if cold, the p95 shifts toward the higher bound.
- Fallback policy: if token queues exceed 2s expected wait, route to quantized fallback model (int8) that reduces per-token latency by ~2.5x. Incorporate a degradation score metric in telemetry to quantify impact on quality.
- Canary and autoscale: canary policy for new model variants; autoscale adds burst GPUs via warm pool in ~20–45s. For 30s bursts, rely on reserved burst pool (the 2 GPUs) vs autoscale.
- SLO commitments: can design an SLO that guarantees p95 <= 600ms at committed capacity; call out that p95 during unplanned regional incidents will fall back to best-effort.

Runbook excerpt (ops play):
1) Pre-day: run cache-priming jobs for top 5% of heavy customers.
2) If observed token/sec > 18k for > 20s -> trigger standby burst pool (2 GPUs) and notify on-call.
3) If queue latency > 1.5s -> flip traffic to quantized fallback model via routing policy and notify CS + customer.
4) Post-burst: drain queues, log regression metrics, and review any quality alerts.

I'll attach the longer runbook as runbook-mandrake.md (attached). Happy to jump on a procurement call to walk through the appendix.

—Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
